To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

firms with excessive debt beyond the optimum level experience higher firm risk during the COVID 19 pandemic and the effect becomes more pronounced among firms with poor corporate social responsibility ( CSR) performance.

firms with excessive debt and poor CSR performance experienced high firm risk and poor performance during the COVID 19 pandemic, and the effect is even more prevalent for firms that are in the high-risk industry.

firms that have a debt level beyond the optimal level and poor CSR practices experience high firm risk during COVID-19, while firms with a debt below the optimal level are self-protected regardless of their CSR performance.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the following questions: (i) how does capital structure affect firm risk during the COVID 19 pandemic?
the joint effect of debt and CSR on firm risk during the COVID 19 pandemic.
the impact of COVID 19 on the joint effect of optimal capital structure and corporate responsibility on firm risk.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the capital structure decision and CSR performance of a business should be in tandem with each other to mitigate the adverse effects of the pandemic.
firms with optimal capital structure and CSR activities are better equipped to deal with the pandemic and are able to mitigate the negative effect on firm risk.

firms with excessive debt and poor CSR activities should be more cautious in their risk management and should consider reducing debt levels and increasing CSR activities.
